research_summary: Stem rust and leaf rust: seedling resistance (all-stage) to all 27 test pathotypes each of stem and leaf rust (ResearchGate IARI Indore newsletter source). High field resistance to stem rust (ACI max 1.5, mean 0.9) and leaf rust (ACI max 3.1, mean 1.6). High adult-plant resistance to stem rust pathotypes 40A and 117-6 and leaf rust pathotypes 77-5, 77-9 and 104-2. The stem rust gene Sr31 is postulated for resistance to all Indian pathotypes, but it is not confirmed as a gene in this variety (CSC release paper). Good resistance reported to leaf blight, Karnal bunt, Fusarium head blight, loose smut, foot rot and flag smut (ResearchGate source). Black/brown rust and Karnal bunt resistance reported by a trade news site (global-agriculture.com). The IARI Regional Station page lists resistance to stem and leaf rust, flag smut, leaf blight, root rot and Karnal bunt. A translated IARI page lists resistance to all three rusts, Karnal bunt, powdery mildew, flag smut and foot rot; this is a mixed-content page and should be treated with caution. Powdery mildew is named only on that mixed-content page and is not corroborated elsewhere.

research_summary: Rust: resistant (PMD_30 and the IPM review list rust resistance; the compendium lists it as resistant; the CSC data describes it as highly resistant). Late leaf spot (LLS): resistant/tolerant (PMD_30; compendium lists it as resistant; CSC data describes it as tolerant). Peanut bud necrosis disease (PBND): the compendium lists it as resistant, while the Purdue table records moderate resistance; the CSC data describes it as field tolerant, so the level is inconsistent across sources. Stem and pod rot (Sclerotium rolfsii) and peanut mottle virus under artificial inoculation are reported as tolerant in the CSC data only; not found in searched sources. The variety was advanced in rainy-season disease nurseries with infector rows where rust and LLS occur naturally (agropedia).

research_summary: Resistance or tolerance claims (CSC record, not linked to a digest URL): resistant to bacterial pustules, bacterial blight, green mosaic and Alternaria leaf spot; moderately susceptible to pod blight; tolerant to bud blight. Seller pages: tolerant to bacterial blight and yellow mosaic virus (YMV) (yashodaseeds.com); resistance to bacterial pustule, bacterial blight, bud blight and Alternaria leaf blight (kisaanhelpline.com, Hindi-language page). Contrary evidence: the AICRP Soybean Annual Progress Report 2024-25 records the highest MLS severity at 77 percent on JS 335 at Sehore, and lists JS 335 as a susceptible check in disease screening. JNKVV states JS 335 is now susceptible to many biotic stresses. A Business Standard report says JS-335 seed lost disease and pest resistance over time because of a low seed replacement ratio of about 10-12 percent. Overall, the resistance claims are inconsistent with the official and press evidence.

name: Yellow mosaic virus
official_quote: RESISTANT TO YMV, RRR, BP, CR, CLS AND TLS
research_summary: Evidence is mixed and partly conflicting. (1) Yellow mosaic virus (YMV): the notified-variety table lists resistance to YMV, but a YMV screen of soybean genotypes classed JS 97-52 as highly susceptible (one of three highly susceptible entries). This is a direct conflict and should be verified before relying on YMV resistance. (2) Collar rot: listed as resistant in the notified-variety table. (3) Charcoal rot: the YMV screen rated JS 97-52 as moderately resistant to charcoal rot (a CR check); a separate field study classed it as highly susceptible to a root-rot/charcoal-rot-type disease, but the snippet does not name the disease clearly, so this conflict is unresolved. (4) Rhizoctonia aerial blight: moderate resistance per the notified-variety table. (5) General: JNKVV describes JS 97-52 as a multiple-resistant, high-yielding cultivar. The original variety record also lists resistance to RRR, BP, CLS and TLS; the digest contains no independent evidence for these, so they are not confirmed here.

name: Grain mould
research_summary: Grain mould: CSV 15 is described as having resistance to grain moulds and good adaptability (name-level evidence for CSV 15, not CSV 25). SPV 1746 (rabi) was rated resistant to grain mould in Zone I of an AVHT trial; no resistant entries were reported in Zone II. Fusarium: SPV 1746 showed the lowest Fusarium infection among tested entries in the same pathology report. Multiple disease resistance: CSV 15 is listed among varieties with multiple resistance or tolerance to major pests and diseases, relative to hybrids. Not a resistance result: SPV 1746 had aflatoxin reported above the CODEX limit in one Parbhani sample (22.22 µg/kg), which is a food-safety flag. No disease evidence was found for CSV 25 under its own name. The genetic-gain study reports that the mold-resistance gain relative to CSV 15 was small and negative.

research_summary: Spot blotch (Bipolaris sorokiniana): in a SKUAST screen of 13 cultivars, RSP 561 was reported as resistant; DBW 16, DBW 17 and RSP 561 formed the resistant group and the other cultivars were susceptible. The SKUAST annual report also mentions RSP 561 among lines not susceptible in a wheat-genotype screen, but the text is fragmentary and does not name the stress. Stripe rust: RSP-561 is used as a resistant parent (HD-3086, RSP-561, JAUW-683, HP-45 group) in a field and SSR-marker study of Yr16/Yr24, and the same disease reaction is shown in a field-condition figure for JWBL-3, JWBL-4 and RSP-561. RSP-561 is also listed as a parent in the PMC study on stripe-rust resistance in advanced lines. Conflict: in the PubMed SSR table RSP-561 is scored as susceptible for the Yr24 marker (220 bp allele) while also listed as a resistant parent for Yr16. Rust status is unresolved.
